newsitem.title: USA: Fieldcrest Cannon workers reject union.
newsitem.headline: Fieldcrest Cannon workers reject union.

text.p: Workers at six Fieldcrest Cannon Inc plants in North Carolina have rejected union representation, workers said Thursday.

The organizing effort by the Union of Needletrades, Industrial and Textile Employees (UNITE) failed by 369 votes, with 2,563 votes against unionization and 2,194 for, in balloting Tuesday and Wednesday.
Earlier union polls had suggested the measure would pass. The highly publicized Teamsters strike against UPS hurt the textile union's chances, some workers said.

"The violence and turmoil of the UPS strike influenced me and others," said John Clay, a machine shop maintenance worker employed by Fieldcrest Cannon and its predecessor company for 35 years. "I also thought the union didn't have anything to offer me."
Another employee said many workers were scared by UPS's statement that it might have to shed up to 5,000 union jobs if the strike dragged on, fearing similar layoffs at the textile company.
The vote at the Fieldcrest Canon plants in North Carolina's Cabarrus and Rowan counties was the fourth attempt since 1974 to unionize workers there.
Some 5,500 workers, most of whom work at the Kannapolis plant, were eligible to vote in the court-ordered rerun of a 1991 contest won narrowly by Fieldcrest.

UNITE, successor to the Amalgamated Clothing and Textile Workers Union and the International Ladies Garment Workers Union, accused Fieldcrest of harassing and firing pro-union workers in the 1991 vote.

UNITE already represents about 2,500 of Fieldcrest Cannon's 10,800 U.S. manufacturing workers. The company is the largest U.S. maker of bath products and the third-larget U.S. producer of bedding products, according to Standard & Poor's Corp.
